clue.text: Mould in the kitchen? Heaps scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up, so its letters can be put back together in a new order

blocks.note: the five letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook finds piles of food thrown out and wonders whether mould got in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like fungus on old food; here it is a jelly mould, and Chambers lists SHAPE for such a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the word for a jelly or blancmange mould, and for the pudding turned out of one.

clue.text: Racing vehicle's flipped — Stewart's bashed

indicators.note: a flipped thing is turned over, so in a down entry the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a kart is a small racing car, with the 's kept

explanation.surface: A racing car turns over and Jackie Stewart is knocked about.
explanation.walkthrough: Jackie Stewart is a Scottish racing driver, so 'Stewart's' signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scots past tense of strike, so it means struck or hit hard, as a Scotsman would say.

clue.text: Big shout — duck, trapped by Hall bowling

indicators.note: something trapped by another word is enclosed within it
bowling suggests rolling along, so the letters are tumbled into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written as O

explanation.surface: An appeal goes up as Wes Hall, the West Indies fast bowler, removes a batsman for a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old shout or call to attract attention, a variant of hollo and hallo.

clue.text: One out roaming with gang bones car museum exhibits?

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so these letters stray from their order

blocks.note: a is one
taken as written
a mob is a gang
the ilia are the hip bones

explanation.surface: Someone wanders round with a gang, picking over bones and old cars in a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers collectable items connected with motor cars, just what a motor museum would display; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: School enthralled by boxed pharaonic crown

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so it is held inside the next word

blocks.note: pent means shut in
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A class of pupils gazes spellbound at a pharaoh's crown in its glass case.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the double crown of ancient Egypt, combining the white crown of the south with the red of the north.

clue.text: Smart clothing number, an incidental benefit

indicators.note: one word clothing another wraps around it like a garment

blocks.note: spiff is slang for smart or dapper
NO is the usual abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A dapper outfit wins its wearer some unexpected perk.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product that brings an extra advantage nobody planned for is called this, so it is a near synonym.

clue.text: Lyrical pattern beloved of Mozart? Con this

indicators.note: the clue asks what goes with the other word to make up the name, so that word is taken off it

blocks.note: Constanze Weber was the wife Mozart loved, here in the Italian form of her name
taken as written, the part to remove

explanation.surface: A music student asks which verse form Mozart loved, and is told to study it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con this' means CON followed by the answer, giving the name of Mozart's wife Constanze; 'Con' in the surface looks like 'study'.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem or song is a verse, so it is a lyrical pattern of lines.

clue.text: Freshman abroad in two US states briefly

blocks.note: PENN abbreviates Pennsylvania and AL is the postal code for Alabama

explanation.surface: A first-year student from overseas is studying across a couple of American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' marks a foreign term: it was used in German Protestant universities, not in the US the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records it as a first-year student at a German Protestant university, so a foreign word for a newcomer at college.

clue.text: Observer on fashion, according to worm's eye view?

indicators.note: a worm sees from the ground upward, so in a down entry the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
ton is fashion or the fashionable set

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist reports on fashion from a very low vantage point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the paper that ran this puzzle; it is just someone who notices things.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes note of things is an onlooker, so the word works as a synonym for someone watching.

clue.text: Parts of long weekends I had involved in shindigs?

indicators.note: something involved in another thing is caught up inside it

blocks.note: a fray is a noisy brawl or row, as is a shindig
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the parties they got caught up in over long weekends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shindigs' suggests parties; here it is the other sense, a commotion or brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A long weekend stretches from the end of the working week, so these days begin one, an example not a synonym.

clue.text: Nitwit stands in line for vegetable fibre

indicators.note: one word that stands in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a file is a line of people one behind another
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool queues up to buy some vegetable fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for tow and names prepared plant fibre such as flax or hemp before spinning.

clue.text: Jock's early evening meal dished out with fermented yeast (8, two words)

indicators.note: food dished out is served up in a new arrangement, so the word beside it is rearranged
fermenting works and churns a substance, so these letters are stirred into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot's teatime food is served alongside some bubbling yeast.
explanation.walkthrough: Each half has its own signal: 'dished' works on out, 'fermented' on yeast. Jock is the stock crossword Scotsman, so the answer is a Scots term.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage this is a high tea, the substantial meal with a cooked dish taken in the early evening.

clue.text: Gable features showing ominous goblin with misshapen nose

indicators.note: misshapen means bent out of its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a barghest is a goblin dog of northern English folklore whose appearance foretells death
taken as written

explanation.surface: Carvings on a gable show a sinister goblin with a crooked nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures gargoyles; in fact the goblin and the nose both feed the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the stones forming the sloping edge of a gable wall, part of its architectural make-up.

clue.text: 'Crufty tufty' to beat those unlikely to score much?

blocks.note: to bang is to beat or strike hard
in cricket the tail is the weak batsmen at the bottom of the order, who seldom make many runs

explanation.surface: A rhyming phrase about a show dog's tuft is set beside a jibe at a weak batting order.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show. The answer is a tail with its hair cut square, or an animal with one: the sort of tufted tail seen in the show ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers defines it as a tail with the hair cut straight across, which is the trimmed tuft a show animal might sport.

clue.text: Greetings — 'love' supplants 'power' in the beginning

indicators.note: to supplant is to oust and take the place of, so one letter goes in where another stood

blocks.note: alpha, the first Greek letter, stands for the beginning
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A greeting card where love has replaced power right at the start, like a rewritten opening line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the beginning' sounds like Genesis; read it as alpha, the beginning of the Greek alphabet ('I am Alpha and Omega'). Swap its P for O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word serves as both hello and goodbye, so it works as a greeting, and as an interjection can stand for greetings.

clue.text: Little fox in maize bordering road

indicators.note: a word bordering another runs along both its edges, so it sits on either side

blocks.note: Zea is the botanical genus of maize
RD is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A fox cub hides in a cornfield that runs alongside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another name for the fennec, the small big-eared desert fox of North Africa.

clue.text: Loose tunic, make woven by the book (short)

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands into a new pattern, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
Ez is the short form for Ezra or Ezekiel, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Sewing instructions: make a loose tunic, woven according to an abridged pattern book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The book' is not a manual but a book of the Bible, shortened to its two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the long loose shirt worn over trousers in South Asian dress, as in shalwar kameez.

clue.text: Fuel extracted from coke I run in stoves

indicators.note: the letters placed in the stoves sit inside that word

blocks.note: an Aga is a heavy cast-iron cooking stove, a fixture of British country kitchens
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone tends coke-burning stoves and draws off the fuel they give.
explanation.walkthrough: This is producer gas, made by blowing air over red-hot coke, so 'extracted from coke' is part of the definition, not a hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records this compound as producer gas, a combustible mixture made by passing air through glowing coke.

clue.text: Doctor mostly available if needed following pseudocyesis?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the phrase loses its final letter

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a military doctor
on call means ready to come out when required
F is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. 5f

explanation.surface: A doctor stays on standby in case a phantom pregnancy needs attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Pseudocyesis is the medical term for a false pregnancy; one old sense of the answer is a fleshy mass in the womb mistaken for a foetus.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives an old sense of the word as a false conception, a mass in the womb that mimics pregnancy; the question mark flags the rare sense.

clue.text: Cosmetic stuff: pad roughly coated in dirt

indicators.note: roughly means not done with care, so the letters are scattered into a new order
a thing coated in another is covered all round by it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
muck is dirt

explanation.surface: Instructions for a beauty treatment: dab on with a pad, roughly, and get covered in muck.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a paste of clay or similar applied to the face as a beauty treatment, so a cosmetic preparation.

clue.text: Scots cravat that hurts, with knotted layer

indicators.note: something knotted is twisted and tied up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: ow is the cry of someone in pain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's neckcloth is tied so tightly in layers that it hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists it as a Scots word for a neckband or cravat, literally something laid over the collar.

clue.text: Bruise nose, cut badly

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxer's injury report: a bruised and badly gashed nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is the formal medical term for injuring tissue without breaking the skin, so to cause such an injury.

clue.text: Sport: left winger for Argentina scores after being fouled

indicators.note: a winger plays at the edge, so only the leading edge of the country's name is used
something fouled is messed up, so the letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the first letter of the country's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football report: Argentina's left winger scores after being brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one player; split it as 'left' and 'winger for Argentina', each giving one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a field game played with long-handled netted sticks, so it is an example of a sport.

clue.text: Galleries displaying old trumpet in antique copper

indicators.note: the instrument is placed in the metal word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: aes is Latin for copper or bronze, hence antique
a lur is a long curved Bronze Age trumpet from Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Museum galleries show an ancient trumpet made of old copper.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word denotes a walkway or gallery, especially one behind a castle's battlements.

clue.text: Corner to be found in vacant lets

indicators.note: the letters are to be found inside the words that follow, a run lying within them

blocks.note: the run starts at the third letter of the first word

explanation.surface: A tenant searching empty rental flats for a nook of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a corner or slice cut off something, a fragment or angle of it.

clue.text: Was this rubbish broadcast? Draws veil possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may form something else, so they are rearranged
the answer plus that short word together make up the fodder, so that word is taken away

these three letters belong to the fodder but not to the answer

explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: 'was' together with the answer is a rearrangement of 'draws veil', so take those three letters out of the fodder before solving.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means foolish senseless talk or writing, a direct synonym for nonsense of that kind.

clue.text: Extreme Pythagorean, as when going aboard the wagon

indicators.note: a passenger going aboard gets inside the vehicle, so the short word goes inside

blocks.note: a van is a wagon or covered vehicle
e.g. means for example, as in 'such as'

explanation.surface: A strict follower of Pythagoras climbs aboard the wagon, sworn off excess.
explanation.walkthrough: Pythagoras taught abstention from meat, so his followers were early vegetarians; the extreme kind avoids all animal products.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoreans shunned meat, and someone who takes that further by avoiding every animal product is a strict vegetarian.

clue.text: Headless ghost, maybe, a bit of excitement historically

indicators.note: a headless word has lost its top, its first letter

blocks.note: something that haunts a place, of which a ghost is one example

explanation.surface: A headless ghost, the sort that turns up in old tales, gives a historic thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Historically' marks an obsolete word: Spenser-era English for an adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic form of adventure, and an adventure is an exciting episode, so the obsolete word fits the phrase.

clue.text: Plots in SA requiring cool courage, first to last

explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa an erf is a building plot, and this is its plural, so it means plots of land there.

clue.text: Some children nervously lost race

clue.text: Some shapeless old stakes

clue.text: Commit to memory an affliction, time inside

clue.text: Old reptile: start of genus is in a path one retraced

the first letter of this word

clue.text: Successful sci-fi writer, even skilful once

clue.text: Treat for type of rot what inky sea has spoiled

clue.text: Legal intermediary implicated in crimes? Never!

blocks.note: the run starts at the fourth letter of the first word
